cues.text: ForkSysInfo is a C client and server built with a Makefile.
This English walkthrough uses the same console evidence and diagrams as the report.
The parent accepts each TCP connection and forks one child process.
Each child serves its client while the parent keeps accepting connections.
Both programs dynamically link the shared utility library.
Each frame starts with a four-byte, big-endian payload length.
Lengths must be between one and four thousand ninety-six bytes.
Read loops handle partial TCP reads before processing.
The SYSINFO request returns the host name, kernel, architecture, memory, and uptime.
cues.speech: The sys info request returns the host name, kernel, architecture, memory, and uptime.

cues.text: PING and ECHO are also shown here, with replies from separate worker processes.

chapters.title: Concurrency: twelve clients and twelve children

cues.text: Twelve C clients request a three-second sleep at the same time.
The process snapshot shows twelve children sharing parent process 2152.
cues.speech: The process snapshot shows twelve children sharing parent process twenty-one fifty-two.

cues.text: All clients finish in 3.175 seconds, demonstrating concurrent service.
cues.speech: All clients finish in three point one seven five seconds, demonstrating concurrent service.

chapters.title: Robustness: fragmented input, idle clients, zombies

cues.text: Three comparisons use the same abnormal inputs with robustness enabled and disabled.
Fragmented requests succeed with read loops. The idle timeout releases a stalled worker.
Reaping removes completed children. The unsafe version leaves a blocked worker and a zombie.

chapters.title: Two debug controls and shared-library linkage

cues.text: Debug messages appear only when compile-time debug and the runtime flag are both enabled.
The linkage commands show both programs loading the same local shared library.
